title: Keep your discharge instructions readable after physical therapy
summary: An original question sheet for organizing clinician instructions; no rehabilitation program or discharge decision is provided.
author: Form editorial source author (AI-assisted)

sections.heading: Keep the boundary in writing
paragraphs: CDC advises people with chronic conditions or disabilities to consult a professional about appropriate types and amounts of activity. That general advice does not describe your discharge decision.

If you have been cleared to transition toward ordinary fitness, keep the scope of that clearance with your written instructions. A remembered phrase such as “you can exercise” may leave important limits unstated. Ask the clinician who knows your case to clarify them.

sections.heading: Create an instruction index
paragraphs: Use a folder or a paper cover sheet to list the instructions you received, their dates and who gave them. Separate current instructions from an older version rather than merging them into a new plan of your own.

If two documents appear to conflict, mark the exact wording and ask the responsible professional. This article cannot decide which instruction should control, and a fitness app cannot silently resolve that conflict.

sections.heading: Take concrete questions to follow-up
paragraphs: Write questions in a way that allows a specific answer. Instead of asking whether all exercise is safe, describe the activity or environment you are considering. Record the response and any limits in the clinician’s words.
checklist: Which instructions remain current after discharge?
Does clearance apply to the activity I am considering?
What should prompt contacting you, and how should I do that?
Who is responsible for future reassessment?

sections.heading: Let unresolved questions stay unresolved
paragraphs: An unanswered question should remain visible. Do not fill the space with a generic internet routine or a promise that an app can replace therapy. If you need clarification, return to the appropriate care route.

This page offers appointment organization only. It has source-author editorial review, not a clinical review of your situation or a validated transition-to-fitness protocol. Public rollout of this collection requires a separate clinical editorial gate.
